Tracheostomy care. Stoma care, tapes and dressing, step by step.
Step one. Know the tube. Know why a tracheostomy is needed, the types, cuffed, uncuffed and fenestrated, and the parts: the flange, the inner cannula, and on cuffed tubes, the cuff and pilot balloon.

Step two. Know the complications: obstruction, accidental decannulation, bleeding, and infection. Know the emergency actions, keep the emergency kit at the bedside, and spot respiratory distress early.
Step three. Keep the airway clear. Know the correct suctioning depth, duration and frequency. Use humidification and oxygen as prescribed, and work with respiratory therapy and the E N T team.

Step four. To prepare, check the physician's order and confirm the patient with two identifiers, as per R M S policy. Explain the procedure, to the family if the patient is unconscious. Organise the equipment, provide privacy, and sit the patient up in semi-Fowler's position.
Step five. Put on unsterile gloves and remove the soiled dressing from around the tube.
Step six. Critical point. Hold the tube in place the whole time. If the tape is soiled, untie it and replace it immediately. Two people may help with this step.

Step seven. Critical point. Remove the unsterile gloves, wash your hands, and put on sterile gloves. Clean the area with antibacterial solution and normal saline. Never let the solution enter the tracheostomy.

Step eight. Replace the dressing, using Sofratulle if it is ordered. An infected wound may be cleaned with antiseptic, then dried. Leave the patient comfortable, clear the trolley, remove your gloves, and wash your hands.
Step nine. Stay calm and reassuring, watch the patient's breathing closely and respond to any change, show empathy and respect, and keep strict infection control.

Step ten. Document cleaning, suctioning, and dressing changes in the electronic record. Record the tube type, size, and condition, the stoma site, and the amount, colour, consistency and odour of secretions. Report bleeding, infection, or displacement promptly, and hand over at every shift change.
